source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 15ης Νοεμβρίου — «Άγιοι Ιουστίνος και Θεοδώρα οι ευσεβείς βασιλείς»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 15 Νοεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. **The page opens by saying it is confused about who is kept here** — «Εδώ τα πράγματα είναι λίγο συγκεχυμένα. Άλλες πήγες αναφέρουν αυτή τη μέρα τη μνήμη Ιουστινιανού και Θεοδώρας και άλλες Ιουστίνου και Ευφημίας»: other sources put the memory of Justinian and Theodora on this day and others that of Justin and Euphemia. It then settles on Justin — «Πάντως όσο αφορά τον Ιουστίνο» — and gives him a full account: of Thrace, before that a herdsman of sheep and swine, then a soldier, then a count, and at the last emperor in 518; his wife one Lupicia, whom he made Augusta and renamed **Euphemia**, and after her death another wife named Theodora; unlettered, but he set the state in order and was a very pious Christian king who helped the Church in every way; he reigned nine years and thirty-three days. **So Justin is drafted and Theodora is not.** The page's own confusion falls on her and not on him: it names three women for the day's second place, Theodora, Euphemia and Lupicia-renamed-Euphemia, and it does not say which the calendar keeps. The corpus already holds `theodora-the-empress` (Greek 11/2) and `justinian-the-great` (Romanian 2/8), and neither is proposed anything here. **No `dates` proposed**: 518 is the year of his accession, not of his birth or death, and the nine years and thirty-three days are a length of reign; nothing is inferred from either. No `locations` and no hymn. The display name takes Thrace because the page says he came from there and because the rank belongs in `types` and `office`. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page.
